title: Towards Trajectory Anomaly Detection: a Fine-Grained and Noise-Resilient Framework

problem.claim: Trajectory anomaly detection seeks to identify trajectory patterns that significantly deviate from normal behavior.

gap.claim: Existing research gives limited attention to fine-grained anomalies and tends to disregard trajectory noise, leaving a gap in robust, generalizable detection for noisy environments.

narrative_sequence.summary: Trajectory anomaly detection is important for identifying deviations from normal behavior in urban computing.
Real-world trajectories contain diverse anomalies and unavoidable noise.
Prior work emphasizes coarse-grained anomalies, overlooks fine-grained anomalies and noise effects, and therefore leaves robust detection in noisy environments unresolved.

source_observation.claim: Trajectory data can contain both diverse anomaly types and unavoidable noise.

interpretation.claim: Anomaly detection methods may need to address anomaly granularity and noise robustness together.

application.claim: When designing trajectory anomaly detection systems, evaluate fine-grained anomaly coverage under noisy conditions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this evaluation strategy is effective or generalizes beyond the described gap.

unknowns: The proposed framework or method is not described.
The fine-grained anomaly definitions and detection procedure are not specified.
No datasets, baselines, metrics, experimental results, or quantitative findings are provided.
